```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 6, fig.height = 3.5)
```

```{r setup, message = FALSE}
library(herminR)
```

MPI assumes every factor can range over the full coded cube. When part of that
region is infeasible, only part of the influence can actually be attained
(referee W2).

```{r}
b <- c(x1 = 1, x2 = 0.5, "x1:x2" = 0.6, "x1^2" = -0.2, "x2^2" = 0.3)
mpi_feasible(b, region = list(x2 = c(-0.5, 0.5)))
```

For rectangular regions the computation is exact. For any other shape, pass a
`constraint` function and use sampling; the sampled maximum is a lower
estimate that tightens as `size` grows.

```{r}
mpi_feasible(b, constraint = function(d) d$x1 + d$x2 <= 0,
             method = "grid", size = 81^2)
```
